title: Three-dimensional QCA that are not stably circuits
abstract: We prove that the three-dimensional chiral $\Z_p$ Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun--Yang--Wang--Tantivasadakarn--Chen are, for every odd prime $p$, not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such statements were known only inside the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated. The key ingredient is a new invariant of invertible subalgebras, which we conjecture to be the square of the total quantum dimension of the hosted anyon theory, modulo rational squares.
summary: This theoretical paper proves that certain three-dimensional Quantum Cellular Automata (QCA) are fundamentally complex, as they cannot be reduced to simple quantum circuits. The authors achieve this by developing a novel algebraic invariant, $I(B)$, derived from the boundary algebra, which yields a non-zero value for these specific QCA, demonstrating their non-trivial nature.
main_problem: The paper aims to determine which three-dimensional Quantum Cellular Automata (QCA) are fundamentally distinct from those generated by finite-depth quantum circuits or simple translations.
main_result: The chiral $\mathbb{Z}_p$ QCA for any odd prime $p$ is proven not to be stably equivalent to a quantum circuit, implying the group of such QCA is not finitely generated.
method: The proof introduces and utilizes a novel invariant, $I(B)$, defined for invertible subalgebras, which is conjectured to relate to the square of the total quantum dimension of the hosted anyon theory.
model_or_system: The study focuses on three-dimensional chiral $\mathbb{Z}_p$ Clifford quantum cellular automata ($\alpha_{p,k}$) acting on lattices, which host specific anyon theories.
key_observables: The invariant $I(B) \in \mathbb{Q}^{>0}/\mathbb{Q}^2_{>0}$, which is computed to be $[p] \neq 0$ for the specific QCA.
important_parameters: The odd prime $p$ defining the $\mathbb{Z}_p$ structure, and the dimension $d=3$ of the QCA.
main_assumptions: The key invariant $I(B)$ is conjectured to be the square of the total quantum dimension of the hosted anyon theory, modulo rational squares.
paper_structure: The paper builds from established results in 1D and 2D QCA novelty, introduces the boundary algebra invariant $\partial\alpha$ related to the Brauer group, develops the specific invariant $I(B)$ for invertible subalgebras, and finally applies this invariant to prove the non-triviality of the 3D QCA.
why_interesting: The work connects topological order (anyon theories) and algebraic invariants (Brauer group) to the classification of quantum dynamics, which is central to understanding exotic phases of matter in strongly correlated systems.
